summary: Kertomuksia III by Josefina Wettergrund is a collection of short stories written in the late 19th century. The tales blend humor, warmth, and gentle moral insight in Scandinavian rural settings, often touching on music, love, and community. The opening story centers on a wandering musician, Sven, and the Ferner family—especially Olivia, a celebrated singer, and her spirited sister Gerda—moving between parsonage life and small-town society. The opening of the collection begins with Wilhelm v. Braun’s playful preface praising the young writer “Lea,” setting a light, friendly tone. The first story then follows Kulkuri Sven, a kind, music-gifted drifter whose birch-bark horn charms villagers, as he yearns to hear his childhood friend “pikku Viva,” now the famed singer Olivia. We learn of his paimenpoika days at the parsonage, his bond with Olivia and young Gerda, and his clashes with the stern housekeeper Borcka. As the Ferner household travels to a nearby town for Olivia’s concert, they briefly misjudge Sven when they meet him on the road; later in the packed hall Sven is moved to tears by “Kultaisessa kartanossa,” and when the concert ends Olivia joyfully recognizes and greets him.
